name: Tagged-Apps
description:
Builds on Clarkar00's widget but uses the existing Homarr apps and ping plumbing.

Dense app links grouped by keyword, with live status dots. Tag apps with comma-separated keywords in the description, e.g. audio,favourites, plus a number to order them. "Categories to show" sets which groups appear and their order; blank shows all. Pings up to 24 apps per copy using each app's ping URL, so remote services work. After installing, open Configure sources and add a Homarr API key.

categories.label: Categories to show
categories.description: Comma-separated keywords, in the order you want the groups to appear, for example audio, youtube, arrs. Matches the keywords in each app description, case-insensitive, spaces ignored. Write keyword=Heading to show a heading other than the keyword itself, for example public=Alpha, admin=Bravo. The heading keeps the case and spaces you type. Leave blank to see every category this widget can find, with counts, ready to copy.

appSort.label: Order within a category
appSort.description: Apps in a group are listed by name, ignoring case. To place apps by hand, add a number beside the keywords in an app's description, for example media, 20. Numbered apps come first, lowest number first, whichever direction this is set to, and the rest follow by name. Leave gaps such as 10, 20, 30 so an app can be slotted in later. One number per app, used in every group it appears in.

cardSize.label: Card size
cardSize.description: How big each app card is drawn, as a share of the normal size. Everything in the card scales together: icon, dot, name, status line, padding. Pick a larger size for a copy that should fill a wide tile or read well on a phone; the size applies to this copy on every layout of the board. For a size that applies on phones only, see the phone stylesheet note in the documentation.

showCategoryHeader.label: Show category headings
showCategoryHeader.description: Print the category name above each group. Off still keeps the gap between groups, so they stay visually separated rather than running together. Useful when a widget shows a single category and the heading just repeats the tile title.

headerUppercase.label: Uppercase the headings
headerUppercase.description: Headings are printed in capitals by default. Turn this off to keep exactly the case you typed, which matters once you are naming groups yourself: system=Charlie renders as CHARLIE with this on, Charlie with it off.

showStatus.label: Show status dots
showStatus.description: Ping each app shown and colour a dot from the reply. Off makes this a plain link list and costs no requests at all. Everything below this until Show status code needs it on.

statusLimit.label: Max apps with a dot
statusLimit.description: How many apps get pinged, counting from the top. Leave blank for 24, which is the batch width. Apps past the limit still show, just without a dot.

highlightDown.label: Highlight unreachable apps
highlightDown.description: Give a card that failed to respond a red border and a faint red fill, so a service being down reads at a glance rather than needing you to spot the dot.

showCodes.label: Show status code
showCodes.description: Print the HTTP status under each app name, for example 200 or 404. An unreachable app reads DOWN instead.

codePrefix.label: Status code prefix
codePrefix.description: Text placed before the status code, so a bare number is not mistaken for the latency beside it. Defaults to "HTTP " (note the trailing space). Clear it for just the number. DOWN never takes a prefix.

codeColor.label: Status code colour
codeColor.description: Colour for codes that count as OK: 2xx, 3xx, and 401/403. Any Mantine colour. Blank uses gray.6.

codeWarnColor.label: Status code colour: questionable
codeWarnColor.description: Colour for other 4xx and 5xx codes, which answered but are unhappy. Blank uses orange.6.

codeErrColor.label: Status code colour: error
codeErrColor.description: Colour for anything outside 1xx-5xx. Blank uses red.6. Unreachable apps read DOWN and are always red regardless.

showLatency.label: Show ping latency
showLatency.description: Print how long the ping took, beside the status code. A service answering in 800 ms instead of 6 ms is degraded, which a green dot alone will not tell you.

latencyColor.label: Latency colour
latencyColor.description: Colour below the warning threshold. Blank uses gray.6.

latencyWarnMs.label: Latency warning threshold (ms)
latencyWarnMs.description: Latency at or above this switches to the warning colour. Blank uses 300. Enter 0 to turn the band off.

latencyWarnColor.label: Latency colour: warning
latencyWarnColor.description: Used at or above the warning threshold. Blank uses blue.4.

latencyBadMs.label: Latency bad threshold (ms)
latencyBadMs.description: Latency at or above this switches to the bad colour. Blank uses 1000. Enter 0 to turn the band off. Should be higher than the warning threshold.

latencyBadColor.label: Latency colour: bad
latencyBadColor.description: Used at or above the bad threshold. Blank uses yellow.6.

statusAlignRight.label: Align status line right
statusAlignRight.description: Push the status code and latency to the right edge of the card. They move together, since they share one line under the app name.

hoverUnderline.label: Underline name on hover
hoverUnderline.description: Underline the app name when you hover its card, so it reads as clickable. Homarr's sandbox blocks every other hover effect.

clickToOpen.label: Cards open the app
clickToOpen.description: On, each card is a link to the app. Off makes this a read-only list: no link, no pointer cursor, no hover underline, so the widget shows what you run without anyone being able to click through. Turning this off also makes the two options below do nothing.

openInNewTab.label: Open in a new tab
openInNewTab.description: On, a card opens the app in a new browser tab and leaves your board where it is. Off replaces the board in the current tab, so you come back with the browser's back button. Needs Cards open the app to be on.

showNewTabIcon.label: Mark links that open a new tab
showNewTabIcon.description: Put a small faded arrow at the right edge of every card, the usual sign that a link leaves the page. Costs one element per card, which counts against the render budget on a long list. Needs both options above to be on, and does nothing otherwise.

scrollWhenTall.label: Scroll when the list is too tall
scrollWhenTall.description: Show a scrollbar if the apps do not fit the tile. Off clips instead, which is tidier on a tile you have already sized to fit, but hides anything past the bottom edge.
